feedback.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-3,4,1)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
${\begin{aligned}x=-1+2t \\ y=5+3t \\ z=7-t\end{aligned}.$

{{field-1}}$\,x\,+\,$
{{field-2}}
$y\,-\,z\,-\,$
{{field-3}}
$=0$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨-3,4,1⟩.$ From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨2,3,-1⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨2,3,-1⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,3,-1⟩ & =⟨-3,4,1⟩\cdot ⟨2,3,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,3,-1⟩ & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨2,3,-1⟩ & =5 \\ 2x+3y-z & =5 \\ 2x+3y-z-5 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
